name: Yoking the mind to Oṃ (as stated in the Kārikā)
method_summary: Know Oṃ quarter by quarter, as the measures (1.24); yoke the mind to the praṇava, which is fearless brahman (1.25); know it as the Lord in the heart of all and as all-pervading (1.28). The text gives no procedure beyond this yoking and knowing.

name: Fixing memory on non-duality (Kārikā 2.36)
method_summary: Knowing the non-dual thus, one fixes (yojayet) memory (smṛti) on non-duality; having reached it, one goes about the world like a dullard (jaḍavat). The text gives no further method.

name: Restraint of the mind (manonigraha) in the Kārikā
method_summary: The Kārikā makes fearlessness, ending of sorrow, awakening and peace depend on restraint of the mind (3.40); to be done patiently, without weariness (3.41), by a means; distraction in desire and enjoyment is restrained and laya treated like desire (3.42); remember that all is sorrow and that all is unborn (3.43); awaken the mind in laya, calm it when distracted, know the mind as sakaṣāya, do not stir it at evenness (3.44); do not relish the happiness but be unattached by discernment and unify the mind (3.45); when the mind is neither absorbed nor distracted, that is brahman (3.46).

warnings.text: yogino bibhyati hy asmād abhaye bhayadarśinaḥ (3.39: yogins fear the contactless yoga, seeing fear where there is fearlessness)

signs_of_progress: When the mind is neither absorbed nor distracted, motionless and without appearance, that is brahman (3.46).

name: Asparśa-yoga (contactless yoga)
method_summary: Named at 3.39 and 4.2; the Kārikā says it is hard for all yogins to see and that they fear it. The text gives no method for it apart from the restraint of the mind taught at 3.40–3.46 (whether the two are the same is not stated here).

warnings.text: yogino bibhyati hy asmād abhaye bhayadarśinaḥ
